metadata.title: Development of a Machine Learning-Based Exploit Generation Module for Various Android OS File Systems
metadata.subtitle: Consolidated report - Probationary period 1
metadata.source_note: Reviewed research/evidence baseline shown above. The refreshed submission tag also contains this report and its editable sources; no new runtime or ML result is claimed.

blocks.text: Official title: Development of a Machine Learning-Based Exploit Generation Module for Various Android OS File Systems.

The team's clarified research goal is to investigate ML/AI-assisted selection of existing research materials using Android device characteristics. The official title is retained, while the present probationary stage is a diagnostic and evidence-preparation stage. A trained selection model or a new exploit-generation system is not delivered in this version.
Problem and research question

Research artifacts can describe different device contexts, revisions, operating assumptions and evidence levels. A source file, a diagnostic text and a reproduced observation are distinct kinds of material. Before evaluating a future intelligent component, the team needs an inspectable prototype and a traceable record of what each artifact establishes.

The current-stage question is: can the available Android diagnostic prototype, research snapshots and source records be organized so that an independent reader can identify their origin, scope, limitations and individual contributors? Future effectiveness claims require a separate agreed experimental study.
Objectives and deliverables

rows: Two registered modules, module descriptions and source manifests
204-file import index and a registry of 12 public diagnostic texts
Data-preparation rules, evaluation methodology and limitations
Commit/PR links, 23 real task records and dated screenshots
Trained model, independent evaluation and device-level results

blocks.text: Scope and completion boundary

This report consolidates the current artifacts and plans. It records preserved tests as historical results and recent verification as integrity checking. Android builds, device trials, PoC execution and ML training were not performed while preparing the submission. The three PoC source groups remain one research module, in the repository structure selected by the team.

The project repository and submission version are accessible at <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research" color="#15598B">the public repository</link> and <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/tree/prob-period-1" color="#15598B">prob-period-1</link>. The technical and evidence baseline reviewed for this report is <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/commit/a50c495b30366b298fa8c7990772096c512773f9" color="#15598B">a50c495</link>. The final tag also includes this report and its editable sources in a documentation-only revision.

Android security research spans application behavior, operating-system services, kernel interfaces and storage. These layers should not be conflated. AOSP documents Binder as an IPC system and SELinux as a mandatory-access-control mechanism; a denied diagnostic operation or a Binder observation cannot by itself establish a file-system defect. <link href="https://source.android.com/docs/core/architecture/ipc/binder-overview" color="#15598B">[2]</link> <link href="https://source.android.com/docs/security/features/selinux" color="#15598B">[1]</link>

The ext4 documentation and the original F2FS paper describe different file-system designs and terminology. They provide background for selecting and describing future research contexts, rather than evidence that the team has tested either file system on a particular Android device. <link href="https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/filesystems/ext4/" color="#15598B">[4]</link> <link href="https://www.usenix.org/conference/fast15/technical-sessions/presentation/lee" color="#15598B">[3]</link>
Why the present preparation matters

items: Traceability makes it possible to distinguish an imported artifact from a result produced by the current team and revision.
Dataset documentation exposes source, annotation and usage limitations before model conclusions are drawn.
A visible separation between a local diagnostic prototype and a future research goal makes the current stage reviewable.
Linked tasks, commits and evidence let the supervisor and committee inspect individual contributions.

blocks.text: These priorities are consistent with the emphasis on data documentation in Datasheets for Datasets and on integrity and verification in the NIST Secure Software Development Framework. They are an academic rationale for this stage, not a claim of full conformance or certification. <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8" color="#15598B">[6]</link> <link href="https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final" color="#15598B">[5]</link>

blocks.text: The immediate beneficiaries are the research team and academic reviewers. The current contribution is an auditable foundation for later analysis. No market-size estimate, deployment adoption, accuracy improvement or device coverage is inferred from the available materials.
Android platform context

AOSP's Binder overview explains the IPC boundary used by Android services. It supplies the correct context for the diagnostic baseline. AOSP's SELinux documentation explains why permissions and enforced access-control policy belong in the interpretation of an observation. Together these sources support explicit context recording rather than assumptions based only on a function name or a nominal platform version. <link href="https://source.android.com/docs/core/architecture/ipc/binder-overview" color="#15598B">[2]</link> <link href="https://source.android.com/docs/security/features/selinux" color="#15598B">[1]</link>
File-system background

Lee, Sim, Hwang and Cho introduce F2FS as a file system designed around flash-storage characteristics. The paper offers design background and reports experiments on the systems evaluated by its authors. The Linux kernel's ext4 documentation provides a maintained reference for ext4 data structures and algorithms. Neither source demonstrates the configuration, security state or behavior of a team device. <link href="https://www.usenix.org/conference/fast15/technical-sessions/presentation/lee" color="#15598B">[3]</link> <link href="https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/filesystems/ext4/" color="#15598B">[4]</link>
Data and model reporting

Gebru and colleagues propose documenting dataset motivation, composition, collection, intended uses and limitations. This is directly relevant to the 12-source registry: source hashes identify bytes, while labels and representativeness require separate justification. Mitchell and colleagues propose model cards to communicate intended use, evaluation and limitations. The latter is a future reporting framework here, because the tagged repository does not provide a trained Android selection model. <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8" color="#15598B">[6]</link> <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993v2" color="#15598B">[7]</link>
Development process and related infrastructure

NIST SSDF provides high-level practices for integrating secure development into a software lifecycle. This report uses traceability and preserved evidence as relevant process principles; it does not map every SSDF practice or assert compliance. The NVD overview describes a vulnerability-data resource. The syzkaller repository describes a kernel-testing project, and its report tests provide context for the public diagnostic fixtures used by the team. These resources have different purposes and are not interchangeable benchmarks. <link href="https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final" color="#15598B">[5]</link> <link href="https://www.nist.gov/publications/national-vulnerability-database-nvd-overview" color="#15598B">[8]</link> <link href="https://github.com/google/syzkaller/blob/master/README.md" color="#15598B">[9]</link> <link href="https://github.com/google/syzkaller/blob/master/pkg/report/report_test.go" color="#15598B">[10]</link>
Synthesis and research gap

The cited work motivates context-aware interpretation, documented data and explicit evaluation boundaries. The present gap is project-specific: the repository still needs independently checked annotations, available prototype outputs, an agreed test environment and a complete evaluation record. The literature review therefore supports preparation and cautious interpretation; it supplies no evidence that the team's intended ML goal has already been achieved.

The review uses selected primary sources rather than claiming to be a systematic review. Search coverage, publication completeness and superiority over every related system are not established. Bibliographic links are provided in References.

The comparison concerns documented purpose, inputs and evidence, rather than performance. No common benchmark was executed. NVD and syzkaller provide useful reference points, but neither is presented as a product with the same scope as this student project.

blocks.text: Resulting positioning

The project's immediate role is to connect a concrete diagnostic source baseline with a transparent research record. It can refer to upstream materials without claiming their original authorship. Its future intelligent component remains a research objective. A credible later comparison must first define a shared task, observation unit, environment and evaluation material; this report does not invent such results.

Repository evidence: <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/blob/prob-period-1/modules/binder-diagnostics/README.md" color="#15598B">prototype description</link>, <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/blob/prob-period-1/modules/android-poc-research/README.md" color="#15598B">research-module description</link> and <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/blob/prob-period-1/data/diagnostic-texts/manifest.json" color="#15598B">diagnostic-text registry</link>.

The technologies below are compared against the tasks already visible in the repository. This is a record of the current stack and its tradeoffs, rather than evidence that a new technology was implemented or benchmarked during report preparation.

blocks.text: Configuration and alternatives

The Android module records Java 17, compileSdk 36, NDK 28.2.13676358 and CMake 3.22.1. These are declared configuration values, not a list of validated devices. Local SDK paths and generated binaries were excluded from the imported snapshot. The source description and configuration files remain the authoritative record.

A single-language prototype could reduce interface complexity but would not describe the existing JNI-based baseline accurately. A database could support richer querying later, while the present JSON/CSV manifests keep this small evidence set reviewable. Raster images are useful preserved artifacts; editable SVG and Mermaid are better suited to future diagram revision. These are qualitative tradeoffs with no measured cost or speed claim.

No new ML library or candidate algorithm is selected in this report. Model choice remains open until the research question, data and evaluation protocol are agreed. File-system background is recorded through the original F2FS study and official ext4 documentation without asserting deployment support. <link href="https://www.usenix.org/conference/fast15/technical-sessions/presentation/lee" color="#15598B">[3]</link> <link href="https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/filesystems/ext4/" color="#15598B">[4]</link>

The requirements distinguish existing artifacts, documented plans and unverified behavior. Acceptance is based on inspectable evidence. The list is a current-stage research specification; it does not replace a full official university marking rubric.

blocks.text: AOSP's SELinux description supports the need to record security context when interpreting unavailable observations. Dataset documentation and SSDF support the provenance and integrity requirements. These references explain the principles; satisfying a listed documentation requirement is not a certification of the entire system. <link href="https://source.android.com/docs/security/features/selinux" color="#15598B">[1]</link> <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8" color="#15598B">[6]</link> <link href="https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final" color="#15598B">[5]</link>

Open decisions include the detailed target population, actual environment, independent annotation review, complete model-selection policy and the final evaluation material. These are recorded as pending rather than backfilled as completed requirements.
Current artifact architecture

The repository contains two independently described source modules, common documentation, research data registries, evidence and planning records. The shared directory is reserved for components with actual reuse; the presence of a directory does not establish a deployed service or integrated ML pipeline.

Prototype boundary

The Android module contains a UI/coordinator layer, a Kotlin/native interface and native diagnostic/simulation code. Existing JVM, Android and native test sources are stored alongside it. The research snapshot module is a separate collection of source versions and reports. No implemented connection that turns those collections into a trained selection service is evidenced.

The new SVGs document the current repository and do not claim to reconstruct that missing original.

Binder terminology follows the AOSP IPC description. Its role should remain distinct from the later file-system research question. <link href="https://source.android.com/docs/core/architecture/ipc/binder-overview" color="#15598B">[2]</link>

The available prototype is the Android source module <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/tree/prob-period-1/modules/binder-diagnostics" color="#15598B">binder-diagnostics</link>. Its README describes local simulation and Binder protocol diagnostics. A newly verified installable APK, hosted demonstration and current runtime screenshot are not available in the reviewed package. The link therefore provides an inspectable prototype source, with execution status stated explicitly.

Prototype review criteria

items: A reviewer can locate the application source, configuration, module description and test source directories from the tagged module.
The module description identifies the current simulation/diagnostic scope and build-verification limitation.
A later demonstration should record its actual code revision, environment, visible outputs and failures. No success screen is inferred from source alone.

blocks.text: Remaining UX evidence

There is no documented user study, accessibility audit, observed task-completion time or fresh installation test in this version. A later prototype review can check whether operation names, busy states, results and error explanations are understood by intended academic reviewers. Those checks remain planned. The source-level interaction diagram and linked module supply the currently accessible prototype material.

That mode checks records and local artifact integrity; it does not fetch or execute diagnostic inputs.
Reported results that remain unreplicated

The jointly authored Assignment 3 contains parser and text-prototype performance claims. Its corresponding implementation, raw outputs, model and complete split ledger are not in this repository. Those claims remain documentary statements of the supplied report and are not promoted to independently verified project results. This consolidated report does not reconstruct missing trials or confidence intervals.

blocks.text: The existing <link href="https://github.com/Nikeka-git/android-fs-ml-research/blob/prob-period-1/docs/research/evaluation-methodology.md" color="#15598B">evaluation methodology</link> separates source integrity, diagnostic classification, record completeness and future system evaluation. Missing data must not silently become a negative outcome; small data sets require absolute counts and clear denominators. Datasheets and model cards support this separation of provenance, intended use and measured performance. <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09010v8" color="#15598B">[6]</link> <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993v2" color="#15598B">[7]</link>
This report adds documentation and diagrams only. No new Android/ACK experiment, PoC execution, model training, measured device coverage or effectiveness improvement is claimed.
Task board and contribution evidence

The reconciled board contains 23 tasks: 12 Done, 8 In Progress and 3 Todo. Completed records are linked to actual artifacts. Partial work remains open. Retrospective tasks register existing deliverables and do not manufacture historical development dates. The 24 October deadline on submission artifacts is a milestone date assigned during registration; unknown future deadlines remain unset.
